trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.

Going up, the next 9 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,2); going right, the next 7 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (5,2) (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes left.
Going down leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes left.
Going left would force the line onto number 3 before its turn; going down would leave both number 3 and cell (6,3) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up.
Going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Going right would force the line onto number 7 before its turn; going left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes up.
Going left would leave both cell (1,1) and cell (3,1) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes up.
Cell (1,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down.
Cell (6,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up.
Going left would force the line onto number 7 before its turn. So the line goes up.
Number 5 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going right would leave both cell (1,6) and number 8 needing the line next, and it can't do both; going up would cut off the top-right corner (4 cells). So the line goes left.
Going up would leave both cell (1,3) and cell (1,5) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going left would cut off the middle (4 cells). So the line goes down.
Cell (4,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now: it goes down.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
